But def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data permits nonzero remainders: g_00 = -(1 + 2 epsilon phi) + r_00 and g_ij = (1 - 2 epsilon phi) delta_ij + r_ij, with Phi = epsilon c^2 phi. The exact equalities in the remark omit those terms without a zero-remainder or leading-order qualification.

The remark calls the formula “the standard retarded solution with zero incoming data on the slab”, but clause (b) allows t on either side of t0. For the admissible source F = 1, H_1(x,s) = s and u(x,t) = c^2 (t - t0)^2/2, which is nonzero for t < t0. Thus the stated formula is not retarded on the whole allowed interval.

The Statement says that epsilon_*' and C_2 depend “only on C, L and the dimension”, while later prescribing epsilon_*' <= min{epsilon_0, 1, ...}. The data allow epsilon_0 to be arbitrarily small with C and L fixed, so a positive threshold uniform in only C, L and dimension cannot satisfy that prescription for all allowed data.
